samples.summary: `--dry-run` early-returns before the new `parseOutputFormat` guard, so `--format bogus` is still silently accepted on ~9 commands
samples.evidence: The new guard is placed inside the `try` block, but several actions return earlier: `cells.ts:52` (`set`), `cells.ts:86` (`delete`), `cells.ts:129` (`batch`), `docs.ts:135`/`docs.ts:153` (`update`/`delete`), `notes.ts:95`/`notes.ts:114`, `slides.ts:100`/`slides.ts:119` all do `if (opts.dryRun) { printDryRun(...); return; }` before `const fmt = parseOutputFormat(opts.format)` ever runs. Meanwhile `docs create` (docs.ts:102-105), `notes create` (notes.ts:60-64) and `slides create` (slides.ts:65-70) DO validate first because their dry-run check sits inside the try. Result: `wafflebase sheets cells set id A1 v --dry-run --format bogus` exits 0 silently, while `wafflebase docs create t --dry-run --format bogus` exits 1 with INVALID_FORMAT — for the same flag. docs/design/cli.md:732 states `--dry-run` "validates inputs". Fix belongs in the new code: hoist `parseOutputFormat` above the dry-run branch (or move the dry-run branch into the try) in those actions.

samples.summary: Design doc still advertises `--format json|table|csv|yaml`, but `parseOutputFormat` now hard-rejects `yaml` with INVALID_FORMAT
samples.evidence: docs/design/cli.md:373 documents the global flag as "`--format json|table|csv|yaml` (default: json)". `OUTPUT_FORMATS` in packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:7 is `['json','table','csv']`, and every `output()` caller now runs `parseOutputFormat`, so `--format yaml` goes from being silently ignored to a documented-shape error. No yaml formatter exists anywhere in packages/cli (grepped `yaml` across the package — only config parsing hits). Either drop `yaml` from the design doc or implement it; packages/documentation/developers/cli.md:115 already lists only json/table/csv, so the two docs now disagree.

samples.summary: Agent-harness comment asserting `status` ignores `--format json` is now false and is cited as the rationale for a hand-rolled session/config parser
samples.evidence: scripts/agent/hunt-workspace.mjs:15-20 (duplicated verbatim at .trusted/scripts/agent/hunt-workspace.mjs:15-20) states: "It does not work: `status` ignores `--format json` and prints prose ... That is ground-truth defect #9". After this change `wafflebase status --format json` emits `{loggedIn, workspaceId, ...}`, so the documented justification for `resolveHuntWorkspace` reading `~/.wafflebase/session.json` and `config.yaml` directly (and doing crude substring collision checks) is stale. The safety behaviour still works, but the comment now misleads the next maintainer and the referenced ground-truth defect list is out of date.

samples.summary: `ctx switch` duplicates the not-logged-in message literal instead of using the new `NotLoggedInError`, so the two paths can drift
samples.evidence: The diff adds `NotLoggedInError` (ctx.ts:35-41) whose message is `'Not logged in. Run `wafflebase login`.'`, and `status.ts:31` exports the same string as `NOT_LOGGED_IN_MESSAGE`. `ctx.ts:95` still hard-codes a third copy of the identical literal in `console.error`. Design doc cli.md:713 sanctions `ctx switch` staying prose, so this is only a duplication/drift risk, not a behaviour break — but the message now exists in three places with no shared constant.

finding.summary: `format()`'s new throw fires *after* the mutation in every un-migrated command, turning a successful write into exit 1 / INVALID_FORMAT
finding.evidence: Only `status`, `ctx list` and `schema` call `parseOutputFormat` up front. Every other `output()` call site still passes the raw `opts.format` *after* the request has been sent: `cells.ts:66` (`sheets cells set`), `cells.ts:92` (delete), `cells.ts:139` (batch), `docs.ts:104/136/154` (create/rename/delete), `notes.ts:64+`, `slides.ts:69+`, `sheets-import.ts:91`, `api-keys.ts:20/34/48`, `tabs.ts:16`. With the new `default:` branch in `format()` (formatter.ts:51-55), `wafflebase sheets cells set … --format bogus` now performs the PATCH, then throws inside the try block, and `outputError` sets `process.exitCode = 1` with an INVALID_FORMAT body — so a caller/agent sees a failure for an operation that actually succeeded and may retry it (duplicate writes). Previously the same invocation printed "undefined" and exited 0. `api-keys create --format bogus` is worst: the key is created and its one-time secret is discarded, now reported as an error. Fix belongs in those call sites (validate before issuing the request), not in the diff's files.

verdict.reason: The finding's central factual premise — that only `status`, `ctx list` and `schema` call `parseOutputFormat` up front while every other command passes raw `opts.format` to `output()` after the mutation — is false at every cited location. Each named site calls `parseOutputFormat(opts.format)` as the first statement inside its `try`, strictly BEFORE the network request: cells.ts:63 precedes setCell() at :64; cells.ts:96 precedes deleteCell() at :97; cells.ts:140 precedes batchCells() at :141; docs.ts:102 precedes createDocument() at :108; docs.ts:141 precedes updateDocument() at :142; docs.ts:160 precedes deleteDocument() at :161; notes.ts:60 precedes createDocument() at :68; sheets-import.ts:50 precedes batchCells() at :91. The finding's designated worst case, `api-keys create`, is explicitly handled: api-keys.ts:23 validates before createApiKey() at :24, with a comment at api-keys.ts:21-22 stating the validation exists so a bad --format cannot discard a one-time raw key. Decisively, a repo-wide multiline grep for `output\([^)]*opts\.format` across packages/cli/src returns zero matches, so no call site passes an unvalidated format string to output() at all; every one passes the pre-validated `fmt`/`outFmt` local. The post-mutation throw the finding describes cannot occur, and the remediation it prescribes (validate before issuing the request) is already the implemented pattern.
